general_information.Description: This course provides students with an understanding of key concepts, theories and practices relevant to the public relations field. Students are also equipped with the essential knowledge and skills of building and maintaining relationships with key publics and stakeholders in a variety of settings. On top of that, students have an opportunity to research, plan, design and evaluate a public relations (PR) campaign for a real client, then present their campaign as part of the course. Lecturer will use mixed teaching methods including lectures, class discussions, video presentations and problem-solving sessions. Students will be required to apply key concepts and theoretical models to develop and evaluate a PR campaign for a client, then present their campaigns in front of the class.
general_information.StudentTasks: -Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. -Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time -Use laptop in class only for learning purpose -Promptly access the https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/gui/Home for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the history, functions, models and types of public relations. Examine and evaluate the roles of public relations in corporate, governmental and non-governmental contexts.
Identify, analyze, and engage with stakeholders to build relationships and manage conflicts.
Appraise and apply the professional code of ethics for public relations practitioners.
Demonstrate the skills required to conduct research in the public relations field.
Develop a public relations campaign for primary publics in order to meet different communication and organizational goals.

Demonstrate the ability to work independently and collaboratively in academic and professional contexts, applying critical thinking, effective verbal and written communication, and the appropriate use of AI tools to plan public relations campaigns.

assessments.Category: Case study analysis (5 hours at home)
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Individual Assignment: PR Case Study Analysis (800–1000 words) Each student will select a well-known public relations case (positive or negative), from chapter 1 to chapter 10, either from the textbook or another credible source, and conduct a detailed analysis. Your case study report should include: - Case Overview: Provide background on the organization, the context of the situation, and the issue or opportunity addressed. - PR Strategies and Tactics: Identify and explain the key strategies and tactics employed, linking them to relevant PR concepts, models, or frameworks. - Outcomes and Evaluation: Assess the results of the campaign, considering both successes and shortcomings. - Critical Analysis: Critique the organization’s approach, discuss alternative strategies, and evaluate the case in light of PR principles and theories. Note: Students use AI tools to identify and summarize credible public relations cases, clarify PR concepts and models, generate essay outlines and check grammar or structure for clarity. However, students must verify all information with reliable sources, apply PR theories and frameworks independently, and ensure that all analysis, interpretation, and evaluation reflect their own critical thinking. - AI Usage Report When submitting the essay, each student must attach a short report explaining how AI tools were used in the assignment. The report should include: + AI tool(s) used + Purpose(s) of AI use: Briefly describe why each AI tool was used. + Verification and Source Checking: Explain how the student verified information or ensured accuracy and credibility + Reflections on Learning and Integrity: A short statement on how using AI tools supported learning, and how the student ensured the final work reflects their original analysis and critical thinking.

assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions

assessments.Category: PR campaign proposal (45 mins in class and 40 hours at home).
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: This is a group assignment. Students assume they are working for a public relations agency and responsible for devising a public relations campaign for a real-life corporate/governmental agency/NGO issue/cause. This assignment consists of 2 parts. Part 1: Situational analysis - For this assignment, students will conduct a thorough analysis, which examines internal and external factors that can influence the success of a PR campaign. This includes assessing the organization's current position, the public's perception, potential challenges, opportunities, and other relevant factors. They are required to submit a detailed report/proposal that includes the following sections: + Executive summary +Introduction to the organization (Vision, mission) + Identification of PR problem the organization is facing + SWOT analysis + Target audience analysis + Research on media landscape (What types of media outlets/influencers... that play an important role in the campaign, how is the organization/issue portrayed in the media) + Stakeholder evaluation (Who are important stakeholders involved in or impacted by the problem/situation?) + Competitive analysis (How your competitors dealt with siminar PR issue, if applicable?) + Communication challenges and opportunities (Any negative perceptions you need to address, any positive points about the issue/organization...) Part 2: Strategy, tactics, budgeting & scheduling and evaluation - Following the Situation analysis, students will continue with the rest of their PR campaign. For this exercise, students will be required to: + Set goals and objectives + Develop key messages + Develop strategies and tactics + Budget and timeline + Evaluation Note: - Students use AI for brainstorming ideas, generating draft content, creating design mock-ups, summarizing secondary research, checking grammar, and visualizing data. - AI Usage Report When submitting the PR campaign proposal, each student (or group) must attach a short report explaining how AI tools were used in the assignment. The report should include: + Purpose of Use – Describe why AI was used (e.g., to generate ideas, check grammar, draft outlines, or analyze sample data). + Extent of Use – Specify which parts of the PR campaign proposal were supported by AI tools and which were completed independently. + Critical Evaluation – Explain how AI outputs were reviewed, modified, and integrated to ensure originality, accuracy, and relevance. Identify what tasks AI was not used for. + Reflection – Provide a short statement on how AI contributed to learning outcomes.
assessments.Grading Guide: - Type: Group Project Including: Written Report/ Proposal + Presentation - AI Usage report.
